speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you describe when it first started and if it is itchy, painful, or oozing?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap).

Thank you for those details; the family history of psoriasis and the red, scaly nature of the rash are consistent with an inflammatory condition, but the location and the patient's age strongly suggest seborrheic dermatitis. I will proceed with this working diagnosis, but please note that psoriasis is a differential consideration given the genetic history.
